html:
The Turksib is a railway running from southern Kazakhstan north to Siberia, linking Central Asia with the Trans-Siberian Railway. It was built between the late 1920s and 1930.

It was one of the showpiece projects of Stalin's first Five-Year Plan. The idea was simple: bring cheap Siberian grain south, so that farmers in the oases of Central Asia could stop growing food and grow cotton for Soviet mills instead.

The line runs from Arys near Tashkent through the foothills to Almaty, then north across the steppe to Semipalatinsk and on toward Novosibirsk. Thousands of Kazakhs worked on it, often their first factory style jobs, while Soviet newspapers and the 1929 documentary film Turksib celebrated the work. The tracks were joined in 1930. The railway opened the steppe to industry and settlers, and it is still the main rail line of eastern Kazakhstan.
sum: The Turksib is a railway running from southern Kazakhstan north to Siberia, linking Central Asia with the Trans-Siberian Railway. It was built between the late 1920s and 1930.
